newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Trading states refuse Iran access to WTO meet.
newsitem.headline: Trading states refuse Iran access to WTO meet.

text.p: Iran was on Thursday turned down in a bid to attend as an observer next month's first ministerial meeting of the World Trade Organisation, trade officials said.

According to the officials, the chairman of the WTO's ruling General Council told the body that there was no consensus among the 125 members on allowing Tehran to send a delegation to the session, being held in Singapore from December 8-13.
No country publicly objected at a meeting of the Council, called to pursue efforts to finalise the agenda for Singapore, to Iran's presence at the ministerial, they said.
But William Rossier of Switzerland, who chairs the Council, said prior consultations he had had with members established the absence of consensus -- the basis for all decisions in the WTO.
Diplomats said the main objections had almost certainly come from the United States, although other Western countries are also known to be opposed to a WTO role for Iran at present.
Washington is understood to have led a group of states blocking an application from Tehran in September to begin formal negotiations on joining the nearly two year-old body.
U.S. officials indicate they see no evidence that Iran is even close to offering the type of open trading regime it would have to establish to win admission.
Countries like China, Russia and Saudi Arabia -- whose applications are under negotiation -- will be able to attend the Singapore gathering as observers.
